newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner ends talks on U S West terms.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner ends talks on U S West terms.

text.p: Time Warner Inc Chairman Gerald Levin said Wednesday the company has ended its negotiations with U S West Inc's U S West Media Group and will keep the terms of their partnership intact.

Levin said "There was no current need or requirement...to restructure" the partnership, under which Time Warner got a piece of U S West's cable systems and U S West received a piece of Time's entertainment busines.
Time Warner officials, in answer to questions, said the talks had ended for the moment.
Time Warner President Richard Parsons said: "We're not getting a divorce."
Time Warner officials made their comments at a briefing for reporters, hours after the company reported second quarter results.

Time Warner posted a second quarter net loss of $0.09 a share compared with a loss of $0.28 a year ago, while EBIDTA -- or Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, or cash flow -- rose to $1.31 billion from $1.03 billion.
Levin noted that several divisions posted record quarterly cash flow results and said he expected "high double-digit growth to continue" in the second half.
Levin said his immediate objective is to pay down enough debt to raise the comapny's investment rating to BBB and then to buy back common stock.
Levin said the company will sell some of its non-strategic cable systems and will enter into joint ventures on other systems.
Time Warner officials said they met with U S West executives and mutually decided to end the restructuring talks after they saw that they remained at odds over the values on their various businesses.

In answer to a question about the Warner Bros. film business, and especially the box office performance of "Batman and Robin," Levin said the company's films were doing well. Asked whether he felt "Batman and Robin" was a disappointment, Levin said no and said that both the merchandising from the film and international revenues would both be strong.
